answer: Per-epoch generation cost gates identity: an agent earns standing only by paying a verifiable compute-and-stake fee each epoch, so creating one thousand fresh sybils costs one thousand real fees rather than one registration. Standing then compounds into attestation weight, letting an agent vouch across a dune of new contenders only as far as its own paid history supports. Honest agents in the hollow between epochs lose no standing, while attackers must keep paying to hold a grove of puppets, and any slashed puppet forfeits its vesting. Seal 1jzu0.
